evidence.claim: CNAS reported that the average DoD supply chain spans five to six tiers, while DoD loses visibility beyond tier two and prime contractors generally lack visibility beyond direct suppliers.
CNAS argued that a full accounting of program supply chains should become a condition for contract awards, supporting the demand case for supply-chain illumination tools.
Fragmented trade restrictions, investor demands for sourcing resilience, and legal scrutiny of supply-chain oversight create a demand backdrop for compliance, traceability, and supplier-risk tooling.
evidence.source_title: The supply chain illusion boards can no longer afford

Descartes Visual Compliance provides trade-compliance software and trade-content integrations for export compliance, restricted-party screening, licensing, and classification workflows.

memory_update.text: DSGX should remain on the public-candidate watchlist as the cleanest US-listed trade-compliance and customs-software proxy for tariff/sanctions/customs-complexity demand.
ULS and ITRKY belong in the testing/inspection/certification gate lane; later layers should test whether supply-chain transparency and compliance tools are material enough versus broad TIC revenue.

NOTE is a speculative micro-cap policy/regulatory data proxy and should not survive Layer 2 unless evidence shows direct trade, procurement, sanctions, tariff, or supply-chain regulatory monitoring use cases.

Many pure-play supply-chain illumination companies appear private, including Altana, Exiger, Interos, and Z2Data; public-market mapping may require second-order proxies such as trade-compliance software, TIC firms, data providers, and government IT contractors.

The key falsification test for this node is whether policy/regulatory complexity converts into measurable revenue growth for compliance modules, supplier-risk products, certification databases, or inspection/audit volumes rather than remaining a narrative tailwind.

node: Supply-chain visibility, traceability, compliance, and sourcing-resilience tools
summary: Layer 1B expanded the underfollowed public universe around supply-chain visibility, trade-compliance, supplier-risk data, and testing/certification gates. The strongest US-listed or US-traded public fits found in this pass are Descartes Systems for customs/trade-compliance software, UL Solutions for certification and product/supplier compliance databases, Intertek for inspection/certification and supply-chain risk tools, and FiscalNote as a speculative micro-cap policy/regulatory intelligence proxy. Context evidence supports the node: defense supply chains often lose visibility beyond tier two, while trade restrictions, forced-labor rules, sanctions, and customs enforcement create demand for traceability and compliance tooling. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
